faq.question: Can I withdraw 100% of my PF while still working?
faq.answer: No. Under the 2026 scheme you must keep 25% of your eligible balance in the account, so a partial withdrawal can take at most what's left after that. The "100%" in news reports refers to 100% of the eligible balance, which already excludes the 25%. The full balance is paid only at final settlement, for example on retirement.

faq.question: How soon after leaving a job can I withdraw my full PF?
faq.answer: Under the board decision now in force, a full settlement of the PF balance is allowed after 12 months without a job, and the pension (EPS) amount after 36 months. Before that, consider transferring the account to a new employer instead. The member portal shows what you're currently eligible to claim.

faq.question: Do I need to give a reason for a PF advance?
faq.answer: You choose a purpose on Form 31: illness, education, marriage, housing or special circumstances. Under special circumstances, DD News reports that no further explanation is required, though that category is limited to twice a financial year. You need at least 12 months of membership for any partial withdrawal.

faq.question: Is PF withdrawal taxable?
faq.answer: Not if you have five or more years of continuous service; earlier withdrawals of ₹50,000 or more face TDS. Even with TDS, the money is only taxed if your total income is taxable; you can file a return to claim a refund. Transfers between employers aren't taxable.

faq.question: Which is better after leaving a job: withdraw or transfer?
faq.answer: Transfer, unless you need the money. Transferring keeps your service continuous, which protects you from TDS at the five-year mark and counts towards the ten years needed for an EPS pension. It also keeps earning interest: 8.25% for 2025–26.
